reading.body:
Connecticut's publicly disclosed data center IT load totals 8 MW across two facilities, and CyrusOne's Norwalk campus accounts for half of it.

The state has five mapped data center facilities, so three publish no power figure at all. Norwalk's 4 MW and 168,000 square feet of technical space make it the larger of the two disclosed sites. Its SSAE 16 Type II certification indicates audited controls over physical and logical access, which is what regulated and security-sensitive workloads require.

For AI, the binding number is power rather than floor space. At 4 MW this campus is small against the utility-scale sites AI training clusters are built around, and the data records no announced expansion here. The suitability score of 49 rests on only two inputs, published IT capacity and operator type, and the methodology flags announced expansion as missing. That score describes how much is known, not what the site could support.

What the data does not cover is substantial. There is no address, no postal code, no precise coordinates, no nearest airport, and no utility or interconnection information. The zeroed latitude and longitude mean the facility is not placed on the map. A reader can conclude that Connecticut's disclosed capacity is small and thinly reported, and cannot conclude anything about the state's actual data center load.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
